disclosures.value: vector_lanes = 11436 (derived-count), binding stage 0, engine duty 99.708% of that stage's own 7.2e-07 s ANALOG m-pass; 16 of 16 stage(s) analog-bound
disclosures.reason: D31-v2 (ADJ-9): the scan/vector engine is never a swept or declared free knob, and it is sized to the ANALOG FLOOR rather than to the beat. Its width is DERIVED here as the smallest integer lane count for which EVERY stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Both targets come from a PROBE pass in which every vector op is counted and costs nothing, so nothing the engine is sized against depends on the engine. The derivation inverts CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work exactly, so the engine sized here is the engine the run is then priced on. THE CRITERION IS digital-per-stage <= the stage's ANALOG m-pass time: the analog side is the binding term by construction wherever it can be. It does not make the MEASURED beat equal the analog time and cannot — a D29 stage holds one stream at a time, so its analog passes and its scan run in series and the measured beat is their sum at any width (here 7.17895e-07 s of digital against a 7.2e-07 s analog m-pass on the binding stage). Per stage: stage 0: 682/683 cycles, digital 7.179e-07 s vs analog 7.2e-07 s, stage 1: 341/645 cycles, digital 3.589e-07 s vs analog 6.8e-07 s, stage 2: 682/684 cycles, digital 7.179e-07 s vs analog 7.2e-07 s, stage 3: 341/645 cycles, digital 3.589e-07 s vs analog 6.8e-07 s, stage 4: 682/684 cycles, digital 7.179e-07 s vs analog 7.2e-07 s, stage 5: 341/645 cycles, digital 3.589e-07 s vs analog 6.8e-07 s. Every stage's criterion was reachable.

disclosures.value: 16 of 16 stage(s) analog-bound after the derivation; the beat-setting stage 5 spends 3.42284e-05 s on shared_digital/attention_qk against 6.8e-07 s of analog m-pass
disclosures.reason: ADJ-9 asks the ANALOG side to be the binding term wherever that is physically reachable. The derivation guarantees the half it can: the DERIVED scan/vector engine is sized so its per-stage time fits inside that stage's own analog m-pass time. It cannot guarantee the other half on its own, because a stage also runs silicon D31 does not size. ADJ-10 then took the two that used to be DECLARED — the attention fabric's array count and the softmax pipeline's lane count — and derived them against this same per-stage target, so what is left underived is the array GEOMETRY (rows x cols) and the terms that are not engines. READ THIS ROW AS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INPUT, NOT AS THE MACHINE: it is measured on the PROBE pass, where the fabric still sits at its declared seed width. What binds the machine that gets BUILT is measured on the priced timeline and reported under its own name, evaluation.digital_silicon.binding_term. On the probe: the largest term is NOT analog, so no scan lane count could have moved the probe's beat. The terms are itemized in evaluation.digital_silicon.derived_engine_sizing.beat_setting_stage. Terms (union of busy intervals, probe slice): shared_digital/attention_qk 3.423e-05 s; shared_digital/attention_pv 3.083e-05 s; link/o_proj 1.076e-06 s; link/qkv 1.063e-06 s; analog_macro/ffn1 1.6e-07 s. Stage span 6.80329e-05 s.

disclosures.value: probe beat 6.78476e-05 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0248%)
disclosures.reason: The probe pass is where BOTH of ADJ-9's inputs are measured: each stage's analog m-pass time (the sizing target) and this beat (the fallback budget for a stage the criterion cannot reach). The beat is a measurement like any other, so this line is where a reader sees whether it settled. Under D31-v2 the beat no longer sizes any stage that has analog work, so a still-ramping beat can only move a FALLBACK row; the analog stage times themselves are sums of op durations and do not ramp. The beat is read off the same settled tail the priced pass uses (P7.9), so it does not move with the window.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_MULT x 11436, FP_ADD x 11436, M_REG x 11436 — at 22nm. 11436 lane(s) x (FP_MULT + FP_ADD + M_REG): one lane retires one scalar operation of EITHER kind per vector cycle, which is the peak CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work is bound to, so the lane holds both arithmetic units.

disclosures.value: stage 5 spends 1.07842e-05 s on shared_digital/attention_qk against 6.8e-07 s of analog m-pass (stage span 2.21066e-05 s)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10 requires that whatever binds AFTER every composable digital engine has been derived be a REAL limit and be named. This row is that name, measured on the PRICED timeline — the machine that gets built, with the derived fabric, the derived softmax width and the derived scan engine all installed — so it is a different quantity from the probe's beat-setting evidence, which describes the machine the derivation ran against. THE NEXT REAL LIMIT IS THE DECLARED ARRAY GEOMETRY. The largest term is the attention fabric's attention_qk, and it is at the floor ADJ-10's derivation walked it to: the fabric is 8 DERIVED arrays of 32 x 64, so every fold of the call already runs on its own array and another copy of the measured block would carry no fold. What is left is ONE array's own walk — ceil(n / 64) column passes, each costing k + 32 + 64 - 2 cycles, plus the fill/drain — and no COUNT of measured blocks shortens it. TWO LEVERS WOULD, AND BOTH ARE REFUSED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN. (1) A WIDER ARRAY: cim.fabric.cols is what the ceil(n / cols) term divides by, and a wider array would also be a whole number of measured 32x32 blocks — but rows x cols is the geometry the systolic closed form was validated at, bit-exact against OPTIMA's recorded ScaleSim outputs, and the fill/drain surrogate is 3 x rows. Deriving a new geometry would move a VALIDATED law onto an unvalidated shape, which is a card change a human makes, not a derivation (ADJ-4, D21). (2) SPLITTING ONE FOLD'S N ACROSS ARRAYS, which needs a claim about how the K matrix is broadcast and how the column tiles are merged that no recorded reference in this repo covers. So it is REPORTED as the limit rather than derived away (D28: a limit named is a provisioning finding; a limit padded away is not). Terms (union of busy intervals, priced slice): shared_digital/attention_qk 1.078e-05 s; shared_digital/attention_pv 8.003e-06 s; link/o_proj 1.076e-06 s; link/qkv 1.063e-06 s; shared_digital/delta_rule 3.589e-07 s.

The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.

The BINDING class here is shared_digital at 86.142% peak occupancy; a class far below it is silicon this provisioning does not need, and the system-sizing sweep is where that is fixed. No threshold decides when this banner appears — it always appears.

Two tensors of the SAME layer can be concurrent (a routed expert beside a shared expert, a router beside a projection), and when the packer lands them in one macro they serialize on its ADC path. The timeline prices that; this banner is where a reader sees which kind of sharing cost time. The CROSS-LAYER terms are the other half and D29 splits them: within a stage the layers run in sequence for the one stream the stage holds and the measured delay is 0.000 us; across stages every stage fires on the same beat for a different stream and the measured delay is 0.000 us.

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

packing.basis: D27's waste, counted in CELLS: committed cells that hold no real weight, over the committed total. cell_floor_macros is the GLOBAL lower bound ceil(total model cells / cells per macro); a per-chip packer cannot reach it when the layers are split across chips, so macros >= cell_floor_macros is expected and the gap is the price of the chip split, not a packing failure.

pipeline.basis: D29: the pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. tokens/s = 1/beat is the exit rate of ONE token per beat; D = the stage count, DERIVED from the stage plan and never configured; the per-stream rate is 1/(D x beat).

state_bill.basis: D29: EVERY stage holds ALL D resident streams' state and KV for the layers it owns. The per-stage figure is the SAME per-(chip, layer) quantities the memory verdicts are taken on, regrouped by stage — not a second computation (D21): recurrent state is D x P2's per-stream state law, and KV is the SUM over the resident streams of P2's kv_bytes_per_stream_layer at each stream's OWN context, because the streams sit at different decode depths.

disclosures.reason: A1 / D17: the fabric is fully-connected p2p, analytical. Boundary bytes are placed and reported; no queueing, routing or topology term exists anywhere in this mapping.

D17 declares one network law and it is the p2p fabric BETWEEN chips. Activations moving between macros of one chip are carried as DAG dependencies with their byte count annotated and no link charge: no on-chip interconnect law is declared anywhere, and inventing one would be a number no card supports.

This model is priced through the 'llama' carrier: model_type selects the FFN/attention arithmetic, not the model's identity. Owners, labels and the atlas all name 'Qwen3.5-4B'; the carrier is named here so the two spellings are reconciled and not read as a contradiction.

disclosures.value: filled_pipeline (D29): D = 32 resident streams, local batch 1
disclosures.reason: The pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. 32 PP stages from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip); D = the stage count, DERIVED and never configured as a batch (D29 removes batch size from this surface). Decode is independent streams staggered one stage apart: one token exits per BEAT, throughput = 1/beat, per-stream rate = 1/(D x beat), every analog op fires at M = 1 and attention/scan are priced per stream at that stream's own context. EVERY stage holds all D streams' state and KV for its layers, which the evaluation reports per stage and checks against the declared tiers.

disclosures.value: 36 beats lowered (31 to fill the pipeline, then 3 STEADY inter-exit intervals measured)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-6 bounds the lowered window; D29 makes the unit a BEAT. The pipeline needs D - 1 = 31 beats to fill; 5 traversals then complete inside the window and their 4 inter-exit intervals are measured, of which the FIRST is held out (that traversal travelled through a filling pipeline, so nothing queued behind it and its exit is early). The beat is the median of the remaining 3. The declared decode_len (256 tokens per request) never enters the DAG: a request's decode phase is decode_len x D x beat and the evaluation prints it in its extrapolation block, labeled.

disclosures.value: dense (Invariant W, D27): 600 macros, global cell floor 545, waste 9.233%
disclosures.reason: Every bank of every macro holds real weights; waste is the dimension-mismatch remainder (258211840 cells) plus the unfilled tail of a last macro (104857600 cells), and nothing else. Dense packing reaches 600 analog macros where the per-tensor placement reaches 632: 32 macros of analog silicon that held no weights now hold some. The delta is stated here rather than left for a reader to notice. K stacks: 64 in-macro (one accumulator per macro under the k_inner walk) and 192 spread across macros (priced by the existing row-block partial-sum law).

D12 sizes the per-macro digital pool so it NEVER BLOCKS the pipeline, and no card declares a per-element cost for a norm, an activation, a residual add or a short depthwise conv. These ops therefore carry zero time and zero energy, exactly as the pass-1/2 report's 'helper lanes are absorbed into their stage' assumption does. Their CONCURRENCY is still measured and it drives the derived pool width (P4.5), so 'absorbed' is a sized claim here, not a hope.

disclosures.value: 1 (the RECURRENT form), in prefill as well as decode
disclosures.reason: P2.6's delta-rule law has a chunked form, but this model declares no chunk size — model_param.linear_attention.chunk_size is optional and has no default — so P4 prices the token-by-token recurrent form on both phases rather than invent a Q (ADJ-4, no invented numbers). THE DIRECTION OF THE RESULTING ERROR IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and this disclosure does not claim it is. The chunked form's saving is state traffic, and this card prices state traffic at ZERO: no cim.cards.<card>.state_bytes_per_cycle is declared, so state_time_s is 0.0 and the whole duration is arithmetic (see the vector_engine:state_bytes_per_cycle entry, which says recurrent-state traffic is reported and bounds nothing). On retired OPS the chunked form is CHEAPER only for small Q and DEARER above Q ~ 34 at this model's dims — measured against the recurrent form: 0.92x at Q=8, 0.99x at Q=32, 1.12x at Q=64, 1.38x at Q=128. Declaring chunk_size is the fix, and the schema now has the field.

disclosures.value: vector engine at 51.8931 W (composed), charged for the op's own time
disclosures.reason: D32: the shared digital chiplet's energy is now COMPOSED from the measured synthesis library — the engine's block census times each block's own measured power gives 51.8931 W, and an op is charged that power for exactly as long as it runs. Its width is DERIVED here as the smallest integer lane count for which EVERY stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Both targets come from a PROBE pass in which every vector op is counted and costs nothing, so nothing the engine is sized against depends on the engine. The derivation inverts CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work exactly, so the engine sized here is the engine the run is then priced on. THE CRITERION IS digital-per-stage <= the stage's ANALOG m-pass time: the analog side is the binding term by construction wherever it can be. It does not make the MEASURED beat equal the analog time and cannot — a D29 stage holds one stream at a time, so its analog passes and its scan run in series and the measured beat is their sum at any width (here 3.38947e-07 s of digital against a 3.4e-07 s analog m-pass on the binding stage). Per stage: stage 0: 322/322 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s, stage 1: 322/322 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s, stage 2: 322/322 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s, stage 4: 322/323 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s, stage 5: 322/323 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s, stage 6: 322/323 cycles, digital 3.389e-07 s vs analog 3.4e-07 s. Every stage's criterion was reachable.

It cannot guarantee the other half on its own, because a stage also runs silicon D31 does not size. ADJ-10 then took the two that used to be DECLARED — the attention fabric's array count and the softmax pipeline's lane count — and derived them against this same per-stage target, so what is left underived is the array GEOMETRY (rows x cols) and the terms that are not engines. READ THIS ROW AS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INPUT, NOT AS THE MACHINE: it is measured on the PROBE pass, where the fabric still sits at its declared seed width. What binds the machine that gets BUILT is measured on the priced timeline and reported under its own name, evaluation.digital_silicon.binding_term. On the probe: the largest term is NOT analog, so no scan lane count could have moved the probe's beat. The terms are itemized in evaluation.digital_silicon.derived_engine_sizing.beat_setting_stage. Stage span 6.77772e-05 s.

disclosures.value: probe beat 6.73562e-05 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0250%)
disclosures.reason: The probe pass is where BOTH of ADJ-9's inputs are measured: each stage's analog m-pass time (the sizing target) and this beat (the fallback budget for a stage the criterion cannot reach). The beat is a measurement like any other, so this line is where a reader sees whether it settled. Under D31-v2 the beat no longer sizes any stage that has analog work, so a still-ramping beat can only move a FALLBACK row; the analog stage times themselves are sums of op durations and do not ramp. The beat is read off the same settled tail the priced pass uses (P7.9), so it does not move with the window.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_MULT x 12153, FP_ADD x 12153, M_REG x 12153 — at 22nm. 12153 lane(s) x (FP_MULT + FP_ADD + M_REG): one lane retires one scalar operation of EITHER kind per vector cycle, which is the peak CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work is bound to, so the lane holds both arithmetic units.

disclosures.value: stage 7 spends 1.07842e-05 s on shared_digital/attention_qk against 3.2e-07 s of analog m-pass (stage span 2.13151e-05 s)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10 requires that whatever binds AFTER every composable digital engine has been derived be a REAL limit and be named. This row is that name, measured on the PRICED timeline — the machine that gets built, with the derived fabric, the derived softmax width and the derived scan engine all installed — so it is a different quantity from the probe's beat-setting evidence, which describes the machine the derivation ran against. THE NEXT REAL LIMIT IS THE DECLARED ARRAY GEOMETRY. The largest term is the attention fabric's attention_qk, and it is at the floor ADJ-10's derivation walked it to: the fabric is 8 DERIVED arrays of 32 x 64, so every fold of the call already runs on its own array and another copy of the measured block would carry no fold. What is left is ONE array's own walk — ceil(n / 64) column passes, each costing k + 32 + 64 - 2 cycles, plus the fill/drain — and no COUNT of measured blocks shortens it. TWO LEVERS WOULD, AND BOTH ARE REFUSED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN. (1) A WIDER ARRAY: cim.fabric.cols is what the ceil(n / cols) term divides by, and a wider array would also be a whole number of measured 32x32 blocks — but rows x cols is the geometry the systolic closed form was validated at, bit-exact against OPTIMA's recorded ScaleSim outputs, and the fill/drain surrogate is 3 x rows. Deriving a new geometry would move a VALIDATED law onto an unvalidated shape, which is a card change a human makes, not a derivation (ADJ-4, D21). (2) SPLITTING ONE FOLD'S N ACROSS ARRAYS, which needs a claim about how the K matrix is broadcast and how the column tiles are merged that no recorded reference in this repo covers. So it is REPORTED as the limit rather than derived away (D28: a limit named is a provisioning finding; a limit padded away is not). Terms (union of busy intervals, priced slice): shared_digital/attention_qk 1.078e-05 s; shared_digital/attention_pv 8.062e-06 s; link/o_proj 1.076e-06 s; link/qkv 1.071e-06 s; analog_macro/qkv 8e-08 s.

The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.

The BINDING class here is shared_digital at 87.824% peak occupancy; a class far below it is silicon this provisioning does not need, and the system-sizing sweep is where that is fixed. No threshold decides when this banner appears — it always appears.

Two tensors of the SAME layer can be concurrent (a routed expert beside a shared expert, a router beside a projection), and when the packer lands them in one macro they serialize on its ADC path. The timeline prices that; this banner is where a reader sees which kind of sharing cost time. The CROSS-LAYER terms are the other half and D29 splits them: within a stage the layers run in sequence for the one stream the stage holds and the measured delay is 0.000 us; across stages every stage fires on the same beat for a different stream and the measured delay is 0.000 us.

disclosures.reason: A macro holds several K blocks of one output block, so their partials must be summed, but the placement that produced them is 'dense' and only the dense packer emits the KStack descriptor P7.2's accumulator law prices. The adds are therefore NOT in this timeline. Pack densely (mapping.packing: dense) to price them; the gap is disclosed rather than silently absorbed.

disclosures.value: 31 fill beats before 3 measured steady beats
disclosures.reason: D29's pipeline is full only after every stage has a stream, which takes D - 1 = 31 beats. The window lowers 36 beats: the fill is IN the DAG (its contention is priced like any other) and the beat is read from the exits of the completed traversals, whose intervals are printed one by one in the pipeline block so a reader can see the convergence rather than trust an average. Streams that enter too late to finish inside the window are lowered as far as the window reaches and their partial work is on the timeline, contending, exactly as it would in the machine.

P3 places; P4 prices (A1). Every op in the emitted DAG carries a zero duration and the annotation P4's pricing table needs. A number here would be a second accounting of a metric P4 owns (D21).

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (3 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Nothing here is a period times a count.

entries.label: per-stream token rate
entries.basis: 1 / (D x beat) with D = 32 resident streams (D29). A stream gets the machine once every D beats, which is the price of keeping the pipeline full.

entries.label: resident streams D (= pipeline stages)
entries.basis: the stage count, DERIVED from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip). D29 makes D a consequence of the stage plan, never a configured batch — the serving surface refuses a batch by name.

entries.label: per-token latency (one stream's traversal of the pipeline)
entries.basis: finish of traversal 4's last op minus the issue of its first, both read off the one timeline: the wall time one stream needs to walk every stage and emit one token. D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

extrapolation.basis: DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

extrapolation.basis: DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. This is an EXTRAPOLATION — a period times a count — so it lives here, labeled, and never enters metrics[] (P4 3, ADJ-6). Prefill is not in it: D25/D29 make the mapped run decode-only and the streams arrive already prefilled.

metrics.headline_basis: ADJ-6: tokens/s at the decode terminal, read off THIS candidate's own timeline (fws_eval.evaluate_fws over program.fws_build's placed DAG). No closed form and no period is involved anywhere in this row.

silicon.basis: 1280 enumerated analog macro slots x macro_footprint_mm2 5.61226 + 2 shared digital chiplets x the card's COMPOSED area 34.9472 mm2 (D32: measured 22nm synthesis blocks, unit counts x measured area, no overhead) + 1280 per-macro digital pools x the COMPOSED pool area 0.00391554 mm2 (D32, same measured library). The analog term is the P3.6 atlas's enumerated_macro_silicon (slots the machine HAS), NOT CimDeviceModel.total_area_mm2 (arrays a model NEEDS).

packing.basis: D27's waste, counted in CELLS: committed cells that hold no real weight, over the committed total. cell_floor_macros is the GLOBAL lower bound ceil(total model cells / cells per macro); a per-chip packer cannot reach it when the layers are split across chips, so macros >= cell_floor_macros is expected and the gap is the price of the chip split, not a packing failure.

pipeline.basis: D29: the pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. tokens/s = 1/beat is the exit rate of ONE token per beat; D = the stage count, DERIVED from the stage plan and never configured; the per-stream rate is 1/(D x beat).

state_bill.basis: D29: EVERY stage holds ALL D resident streams' state and KV for the layers it owns. The per-stage figure is the SAME per-(chip, layer) quantities the memory verdicts are taken on, regrouped by stage — not a second computation (D21): recurrent state is D x P2's per-stream state law, and KV is the SUM over the resident streams of P2's kv_bytes_per_stream_layer at each stream's OWN context, because the streams sit at different decode depths.

disclosures.reason: A1 / D17: the fabric is fully-connected p2p, analytical. Boundary bytes are placed and reported; no queueing, routing or topology term exists anywhere in this mapping.

D17 declares one network law and it is the p2p fabric BETWEEN chips. Activations moving between macros of one chip are carried as DAG dependencies with their byte count annotated and no link charge: no on-chip interconnect law is declared anywhere, and inventing one would be a number no card supports.

This model is priced through the 'llama' carrier: model_type selects the FFN/attention arithmetic, not the model's identity. Owners, labels and the atlas all name 'Qwen3.5-4B'; the carrier is named here so the two spellings are reconciled and not read as a contradiction.

disclosures.value: filled_pipeline (D29): D = 2 resident streams, local batch 1
disclosures.reason: The pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. 2 PP stages from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip); D = the stage count, DERIVED and never configured as a batch (D29 removes batch size from this surface). Decode is independent streams staggered one stage apart: one token exits per BEAT, throughput = 1/beat, per-stream rate = 1/(D x beat), every analog op fires at M = 1 and attention/scan are priced per stream at that stream's own context. EVERY stage holds all D streams' state and KV for its layers, which the evaluation reports per stage and checks against the declared tiers.

disclosures.value: 6 beats lowered (1 to fill the pipeline, then 3 STEADY inter-exit intervals measured)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-6 bounds the lowered window; D29 makes the unit a BEAT. The pipeline needs D - 1 = 1 beats to fill; 5 traversals then complete inside the window and their 4 inter-exit intervals are measured, of which the FIRST is held out (that traversal travelled through a filling pipeline, so nothing queued behind it and its exit is early). The beat is the median of the remaining 3. The declared decode_len (256 tokens per request) never enters the DAG: a request's decode phase is decode_len x D x beat and the evaluation prints it in its extrapolation block, labeled.

disclosures.value: dense (Invariant W, D27): 632 macros, global cell floor 545, waste 13.829%
disclosures.reason: Every bank of every macro holds real weights; waste is the dimension-mismatch remainder (572784640 cells) plus the unfilled tail of a last macro (0 cells), and nothing else. This packing IS the dedicated placement (0 macros saved): the degenerate identity holds and every number downstream is the one today's placement produces. K stacks: 0 in-macro (one accumulator per macro under the k_inner walk) and 64 spread across macros (priced by the existing row-block partial-sum law).

D12 sizes the per-macro digital pool so it NEVER BLOCKS the pipeline, and no card declares a per-element cost for a norm, an activation, a residual add or a short depthwise conv. These ops therefore carry zero time and zero energy, exactly as the pass-1/2 report's 'helper lanes are absorbed into their stage' assumption does. Their CONCURRENCY is still measured and it drives the derived pool width (P4.5), so 'absorbed' is a sized claim here, not a hope.

disclosures.value: 1 (the RECURRENT form), in prefill as well as decode
disclosures.reason: P2.6's delta-rule law has a chunked form, but this model declares no chunk size — model_param.linear_attention.chunk_size is optional and has no default — so P4 prices the token-by-token recurrent form on both phases rather than invent a Q (ADJ-4, no invented numbers). THE DIRECTION OF THE RESULTING ERROR IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and this disclosure does not claim it is. The chunked form's saving is state traffic, and this card prices state traffic at ZERO: no cim.cards.<card>.state_bytes_per_cycle is declared, so state_time_s is 0.0 and the whole duration is arithmetic (see the vector_engine:state_bytes_per_cycle entry, which says recurrent-state traffic is reported and bounds nothing). On retired OPS the chunked form is CHEAPER only for small Q and DEARER above Q ~ 34 at this model's dims — measured against the recurrent form: 0.92x at Q=8, 0.99x at Q=32, 1.12x at Q=64, 1.38x at Q=128. Declaring chunk_size is the fix, and the schema now has the field.

Stage 0 is binding at a 6.08e-06 s analog m-pass and the engine runs at 99.931% duty inside it; 2 of 2 stage(s) are analog-bound by construction.

CimDeviceModel prices this op with 'delta_rule_recurrent', which carries validated == 'unvalidated': the work counts are derived from first principles and NO numeric reference exists to check them against anywhere (D21). Every number this op contributes to — the makespan, the headline throughput, this device's occupancy — inherits that status. The law is not a guess about the hardware card, which is declared; it is an unchecked count of the arithmetic the algorithm does.

disclosures.value: vector engine at 34.036 W (composed), charged for the op's own time
disclosures.reason: D32: the shared digital chiplet's energy is now COMPOSED from the measured synthesis library — the engine's block census times each block's own measured power gives 34.036 W, and an op is charged that power for exactly as long as it runs. The label is PARTIAL, not COVERED, and here is why: the library reports ONE average power per block and does not separate dynamic from static, so (a) a block's power is charged at its synthesis toggle rate rather than at this op's activity, and (b) the chiplet's LEAKAGE while it is idle is not charged at all — an idle engine costs 0 pJ here, which is a floor, not a measurement. Both directions are named rather than folded into one adjusted number (D21, one accounting per metric).

disclosures.value: priced with the shift-and-add tree law
disclosures.reason: A row-block partial sum and a bit-slice composition are the same adder tree on the same per-macro pool, so they are priced by the same P2 law (price_reduction) with the operand count in place of the slice count. Declaring a second law for one shape would be a second accounting (D21).

cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the priced shift-add trees report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The reduction TIME is fully priced; only its energy is uncovered (ADJ-4).

disclosures.value: three serial DAG ops, not one folded stage
disclosures.reason: P2's attention law folds QK^T and PV into ONE concurrent systolic stage and runs the softmax pipeline beside it: stage = max(max(qk, pv) + fill_drain, softmax). P3 placed three dependent ops, so the DAG prices three ops and SERIALIZES them. The op-internal fill/drain penalty is charged ONCE, on the QK op, and it is never added to the DAG's own system-level ramp — two quantities, two names (P4 §1). On disagreement the DAG wins and the closed form is annotated (ADJ-8); this note is that annotation.

disclosures.value: cim.fabric.num_arrays = 8 (derived-count, declared seed 2), softmax_lanes = 16 (declared seed 1), on the DECLARED 32x64 array x 1 replica(s); binding stage 0, attention time 1234.349% of that stage's own 6.08e-06 s ANALOG m-pass; 0 of 2 stage(s) analog-bound
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10: EVERY digital engine whose width is a composition of MEASURED synthesis blocks derives to the analog floor, not just the scan engine. The attention fabric's ARRAY COUNT is derived here in integer copies of the measured GEMMINI 32x32 block and the softmax pipeline's LANE COUNT in copies of its measured per-lane census, as the smallest integers for which every stage's attention time — qk + fill/drain + softmax + pv, the three ops the lowering serializes — fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). The target is the same measurement ADJ-9 sizes the scan engine against, taken off the same probe pass. ONLY THE COUNT IS DERIVED: rows x cols per array stay as measured and as declared, because inventing array geometry is refused (ADJ-4). THE FOLD LAW: the arrays split into a QK group and a PV group and a call's folds (heads_per_replica x streams) are dealt across the group, so an array in a group of a carries ceil(folds / a) of them; at num_arrays = 2 the split is (1, 1) and the law is the pass-1 law bit for bit. Per stage: stage 0: qk 40596 + sm 80 + pv 30236 (+384 fill/drain) = 71296/5775 cycles, attention 7.505e-05 s vs analog 6.08e-06 s, stage 1: qk 40596 + sm 80 + pv 30220 (+384 fill/drain) = 71280/5775 cycles, attention 7.503e-05 s vs analog 6.08e-06 s. FOLD CONCURRENCY SATURATES on stage(s) 0, 1: past 2 x folds arrays another copy of the measured block carries no fold and buys no time, so those stages take the SATURATION width and the residue — the DECLARED rows x cols geometry's own floor, ceil(n / cols) column passes times the k + rows + cols - 2 pipeline term — is NAMED rather than clamped away. Splitting one fold's N across arrays would shrink it further and is NOT modelled: it is a claim about the fabric's dataflow that no recorded reference in this repo covers.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — GEMMINI_SYS_ARRAY x 16, TRANSPOSER x 1 — at 22nm. ceil(32/32) * ceil(64/32) = 2 measured 32x32 blocks per array, x 8 arrays x 1 replicas = 16, plus 1 TRANSPOSER.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_COMP x 15, FP_ADD x 31, FP_MULT x 32, BF16_EXP x 16, BF16_RECIP x 1 — at 22nm. OPTIMA create_softmax_collection at width 16, instantiated 1 time(s) (one per attention replica, matching CimDeviceModel.softmax_cycles which spends softmax_lanes x replicas).

disclosures.value: vector_lanes = 7971 (derived-count), binding stage 0, engine duty 99.931% of that stage's own 6.08e-06 s ANALOG m-pass; 2 of 2 stage(s) analog-bound
disclosures.reason: D31-v2 (ADJ-9): the scan/vector engine is never a swept or declared free knob, and it is sized to the ANALOG FLOOR rather than to the beat. Its width is DERIVED here as the smallest integer lane count for which EVERY stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Both targets come from a PROBE pass in which every vector op is counted and costs nothing, so nothing the engine is sized against depends on the engine. The derivation inverts CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work exactly, so the engine sized here is the engine the run is then priced on. THE CRITERION IS digital-per-stage <= the stage's ANALOG m-pass time: the analog side is the binding term by construction wherever it can be. It does not make the MEASURED beat equal the analog time and cannot — a D29 stage holds one stream at a time, so its analog passes and its scan run in series and the measured beat is their sum at any width (here 6.07579e-06 s of digital against a 6.08e-06 s analog m-pass on the binding stage). Per stage: stage 0: 5772/5775 cycles, digital 6.076e-06 s vs analog 6.08e-06 s, stage 1: 5772/5775 cycles, digital 6.076e-06 s vs analog 6.08e-06 s. Every stage's criterion was reachable.

disclosures.value: 2 of 2 stage(s) analog-bound after the derivation; the beat-setting stage 0 spends 0.000136914 s on shared_digital/attention_qk against 6.08e-06 s of analog m-pass
disclosures.reason: ADJ-9 asks the ANALOG side to be the binding term wherever that is physically reachable. The derivation guarantees the half it can: the DERIVED scan/vector engine is sized so its per-stage time fits inside that stage's own analog m-pass time. It cannot guarantee the other half on its own, because a stage also runs silicon D31 does not size. ADJ-10 then took the two that used to be DECLARED — the attention fabric's array count and the softmax pipeline's lane count — and derived them against this same per-stage target, so what is left underived is the array GEOMETRY (rows x cols) and the terms that are not engines. READ THIS ROW AS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INPUT, NOT AS THE MACHINE: it is measured on the PROBE pass, where the fabric still sits at its declared seed width. What binds the machine that gets BUILT is measured on the priced timeline and reported under its own name, evaluation.digital_silicon.binding_term. On the probe: the largest term is NOT analog, so no scan lane count could have moved the probe's beat. The terms are itemized in evaluation.digital_silicon.derived_engine_sizing.beat_setting_stage. Terms (union of busy intervals, probe slice): shared_digital/attention_qk 0.0001369 s; shared_digital/attention_pv 0.0001226 s; link/o_proj 4.305e-06 s; link/qkv 4.153e-06 s; macro_pool/ffn2 1.297e-06 s. Stage span 0.000276748 s.

disclosures.value: probe beat 0.000276681 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0243%)
disclosures.reason: The probe pass is where BOTH of ADJ-9's inputs are measured: each stage's analog m-pass time (the sizing target) and this beat (the fallback budget for a stage the criterion cannot reach). The beat is a measurement like any other, so this line is where a reader sees whether it settled. Under D31-v2 the beat no longer sizes any stage that has analog work, so a still-ramping beat can only move a FALLBACK row; the analog stage times themselves are sums of op durations and do not ramp. The beat is read off the same settled tail the priced pass uses (P7.9), so it does not move with the window.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_MULT x 7971, FP_ADD x 7971, M_REG x 7971 — at 22nm. 7971 lane(s) x (FP_MULT + FP_ADD + M_REG): one lane retires one scalar operation of EITHER kind per vector cycle, which is the peak CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work is bound to, so the lane holds both arithmetic units.

disclosures.value: stage 0 spends 4.31368e-05 s on shared_digital/attention_qk against 6.08e-06 s of analog m-pass (stage span 9.82388e-05 s)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10 requires that whatever binds AFTER every composable digital engine has been derived be a REAL limit and be named. This row is that name, measured on the PRICED timeline — the machine that gets built, with the derived fabric, the derived softmax width and the derived scan engine all installed — so it is a different quantity from the probe's beat-setting evidence, which describes the machine the derivation ran against. THE NEXT REAL LIMIT IS THE DECLARED ARRAY GEOMETRY. The largest term is the attention fabric's attention_qk, and it is at the floor ADJ-10's derivation walked it to: the fabric is 8 DERIVED arrays of 32 x 64, so every fold of the call already runs on its own array and another copy of the measured block would carry no fold. What is left is ONE array's own walk — ceil(n / 64) column passes, each costing k + 32 + 64 - 2 cycles, plus the fill/drain — and no COUNT of measured blocks shortens it. TWO LEVERS WOULD, AND BOTH ARE REFUSED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN. (1) A WIDER ARRAY: cim.fabric.cols is what the ceil(n / cols) term divides by, and a wider array would also be a whole number of measured 32x32 blocks — but rows x cols is the geometry the systolic closed form was validated at, bit-exact against OPTIMA's recorded ScaleSim outputs, and the fill/drain surrogate is 3 x rows. Deriving a new geometry would move a VALIDATED law onto an unvalidated shape, which is a card change a human makes, not a derivation (ADJ-4, D21). (2) SPLITTING ONE FOLD'S N ACROSS ARRAYS, which needs a claim about how the K matrix is broadcast and how the column tiles are merged that no recorded reference in this repo covers. So it is REPORTED as the limit rather than derived away (D28: a limit named is a provisioning finding; a limit padded away is not). Terms (union of busy intervals, priced slice): shared_digital/attention_qk 4.314e-05 s; shared_digital/attention_pv 3.183e-05 s; shared_digital/delta_rule 6.076e-06 s; link/o_proj 4.305e-06 s; link/qkv 4.153e-06 s.

The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.

P3 places; P4 prices (A1). Every op in the emitted DAG carries a zero duration and the annotation P4's pricing table needs. A number here would be a second accounting of a metric P4 owns (D21).

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (3 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Two tensors of the SAME layer can be concurrent (a routed expert beside a shared expert, a router beside a projection), and when the packer lands them in one macro they serialize on its ADC path. the ladder is a DIRECTIONAL walk from the declared initializer: it prices every point it steps to and every one-rung neighbour of those, and it never touches the rest of the cross product. The label is PARTIAL, not COVERED, and here is why: the library reports ONE average power per block and does not separate dynamic from static, so (a) a block's power is charged at its synthesis toggle rate rather than at this op's activity, and (b) the chiplet's LEAKAGE while it is idle is not charged at all — an idle engine costs 0 pJ here, which is a floor, not a measurement. Both directions are named rather than folded into one adjusted number (D21, one accounting per metric).

disclosures.reason: cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the K-stack accumulators report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The accumulator TIME is fully priced (P7.2).

disclosures.value: priced with the shift-and-add tree law
disclosures.reason: A row-block partial sum and a bit-slice composition are the same adder tree on the same per-macro pool, so they are priced by the same P2 law (price_reduction) with the operand count in place of the slice count. Declaring a second law for one shape would be a second accounting (D21).

cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the priced shift-add trees report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The reduction TIME is fully priced; only its energy is uncovered (ADJ-4).

disclosures.value: three serial DAG ops, not one folded stage
disclosures.reason: P2's attention law folds QK^T and PV into ONE concurrent systolic stage and runs the softmax pipeline beside it: stage = max(max(qk, pv) + fill_drain, softmax). P3 placed three dependent ops, so the DAG prices three ops and SERIALIZES them. The op-internal fill/drain penalty is charged ONCE, on the QK op, and it is never added to the DAG's own system-level ramp — two quantities, two names (P4 §1). On disagreement the DAG wins and the closed form is annotated (ADJ-8); this note is that annotation.

FOLD CONCURRENCY SATURATES on stage(s) 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7: past 2 x folds arrays another copy of the measured block carries no fold and buys no time, so those stages take the SATURATION width and the residue — the DECLARED rows x cols geometry's own floor, ceil(n / cols) column passes times the k + rows + cols - 2 pipeline term — is NAMED rather than clamped away.
